name: PTC India Financial Services Ltd
title: PTC India Financial Services Ltd - 533344 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: PFS FY26 PAT rose to INR319 crores from INR217 crores, while Q4 sanctions jumped to INR1,004 crores and gross Stage III fell 73% to INR190 crores.
summary.overview: FY26 showed a sharp pickup in sanctions (INR3,448 crores, over 4x FY25) and disbursements (INR1,235 crores, up 35%), with PAT up about 47% to INR319 crores. Asset quality improved materially: gross Stage III fell to INR190 crores and net Stage III to INR47 crores, with provision coverage on Stage III at 75%. AUM moderated to INR3,292 crores as low-yield legacy loans prepaid (INR1,105 crores of unscheduled prepayments), and Q4 profitability softened with RoNW at 6.24% and portfolio yield at 10.29%. Leadership change (MD and CEO R. Balaji resigned, effective after 30 June) and the absence of a dividend dominated investor questions.

segments.name: Infrastructure finance (renewable, transmission, DISCOM, oil and gas, roads, CBG, data centre)
segments.commentary: All FY26 disbursements went to private corporate borrowers; sanctions were mainly private, with one or two utility sanctions where returns are acceptable. Structured finance (value chain) is being built to lift yield over the medium term.

segments.name: Stage III / legacy resolution
segments.commentary: Major part of the INR190 crores gross Stage III is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT; promoters have offered an OTS that will be considered on merits. About 73% of gross Stage III accounts by value transitioned out during the year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth (disbursements minus repayments), with quality prioritised over quantity.
About INR2,000 crores of sanctioned amount is undisbursed; roughly INR1,500 crores expected in the next two quarters, with major portion in Q2 FY27.
FY27 disbursement target of INR4,000 crores is not yet set; budget is awaiting approval and is framed on yield and RoA, not volume.
Cost of funds expected to fall as fresh borrowings replace older, higher-cost debt; PFS base rate was cut by 60 bps in the last quarter.
No dividend declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management acknowledged a suggestion for a dividend at the annual meeting.
capex_capacity: Sanctions-to-disbursement gap is structural: infrastructure projects run 6 months to 3.5 years, so disbursement follows construction progress.
Liquidity of about INR1,800 crores on balance sheet; borrowing deferred until required, with ALCO matching disbursement needs.
Average tenure of new project loans cited at 5 to 7 years.
Prepayments of INR1,105 crores and total repayments of INR1,441 crores in FY26; prepayments were low-yield legacy loans and are not predictable.
demand_pricing: Management says new disbursements are at higher yields than prepaid loans, so portfolio yield is expected to improve.
Q4 FY26 portfolio yield fell to 10.29% from 11.27%, which management attributed to portfolio dynamics and calibrated growth.
Sole and multiple lending structures are being prioritised over consortium lending, though PFS also participates in consortium and co-lending on a case-by-case basis.
Net NPA stated at 1.49%, with gross NPA INR190 crores and net NPA INR47 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gap between sanctions (about INR3,500 crores) and disbursements (about INR1,200 crores) so large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said infrastructure projects are disbursed as construction progresses over 1 to 3 years, so sanctions convert to disbursement later. Past lack of a sanctioned pipeline also explains the current low disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did R. Balaji resign, and is the FY27 disbursement vision still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The company said the resignation was for personal reasons already disclosed; the MD and CEO remains until 30 June and a replacement process has started. The FY27 target of about INR4,000 crores was not committed and is pending budget approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why is borrowing cost high at around 9.5%, and what is the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of borrowing is below 9.5%, that the treasury is pressing lenders for spread cuts, and that the base rate was cut 60 bps. Cost of funds should fall as new, cheaper borrowings replace older debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company declare a dividend, and what is the NTPC promoter impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend has not been declared; the board will review it next quarter. Management said no formal intimation on the NTPC shareholding change has been received and no adverse impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company holding cash rather than disbursing, and is this a fundraising issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds about INR1,800 crores of liquidity, will borrow only when needed to match asset-liability timing, and has about INR2,000 crores of pipeline to disburse over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the INR190 crores gross Stage III accounts, and what is the status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kalur Srinivas said the major portion is Danu Wind Parks, referred to NCLT, with the promoters having offered an OTS that will be considered on merits; updates will be given to exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for AUM growth over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 30% to 50% YoY AUM growth, stating that AUM means disbursements minus repayments, and said no fresh slippage has occurred in the last eight years of disbursements.

risks_watch: Leadership transition: MD and CEO R. Balaji resigned with replacement pending; the CEO seat will be vacant once he leaves after 30 June.
Q4 FY26 RoNW (6.24%) and yield (10.29%) fell YoY despite higher sanctions; watch whether disbursement converts into yield recovery.
Conversion of about INR2,000 crores undisbursed sanctions, targeted at roughly INR1,500 crores over two quarters.
Unpredictable prepayments (INR1,105 crores in FY26) could offset disbursement growth and keep AUM flat.
Danu Wind Parks NCLT resolution and OTS outcome, which drive the bulk of gross Stage III.
Dividend decision next quarter, and any clarification on the NTPC promoter change.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 operating momentum and asset quality, but defensive and evasive on leadership change, dividend timing, borrowing plans and the FY27 target, which management said was not yet set.
key_quotes: So our yield is expected to be improving because the new disbursements are being done for a high-yield proposals where the prepayments are being done on a low-yield proposals.
Quality, we have already worked on. There is no fresh slippage in our, say, last 8 years disbursement. It will not happen in future also.
And you'll see at least, say, 30% to 50% growth year-on-year.
